clue.text: Whence military orders may come in poor condition

definitions.meaning: SHAPE is the Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, so orders issued from there come out of it
unfit, as a person who has not been exercising

explanation.surface: A remark about where army commands are issued, then a description of someone unfit.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAPE is NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, so its orders literally come from inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unfit or in bad physical form is the idiomatic sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Exploit having duck on river

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the letter O
to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of a duck floating on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts O above USE. The Ouse is a river in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is a river name shared by several English rivers, one flowing through York.

clue.text: Play securing new theatre award

indicators.note: the toy holds the other piece fast inside it

parts.note: to play with something is to toy with it

explanation.surface: A new play wins a prize on Broadway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tony is the annual Broadway prize for theatrical achievement in the United States.

clue.text: Painting of dead writer and philosopher

parts.note: a dead battery or dead market is flat
Ford Madox Ford, the English novelist
John Stuart Mill, the English philosopher

explanation.surface: A portrait of a deceased author who was also a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Flatford Mill is a famous John Constable painting of a Suffolk mill.
explanation.definitionFit: This Constable canvas of a Suffolk watermill scene is an example of a painting.

clue.text: With heroin, just some can cause addiction

parts.note: H is slang for heroin
just some means a bit, a small amount

explanation.surface: A warning that even a little heroin can get you hooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can cause' is link material leading to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug habit is a compulsive dependency, so the word is a synonym for addiction.

clue.text: He declined Nobel prize, by gum, breaking rank

parts.note: paste is a glue, a kind of gum

indicators.note: the letters of rank are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A man refused the Nobel, broke ranks, and exclaimed 'by gum'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' scrambles RANK into RNAK; 'by gum' looks like the northern exclamation but gum is PASTE. Boris Pasternak turned down the 1958 literature prize under Soviet pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Pasternak, author of Doctor Zhivago, was forced by the Soviet state to refuse the 1958 literature prize.

clue.text: Tree dad noticed in America

indicators.note: dad is seen inside America, the one placed within the other

parts.note: US, the United States
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A father spots a tree while travelling in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a poisonous tropical Asian tree of legend whose sap was used on arrows.

clue.text: Retired couples' addresses very near each other?

definitions.text: Retired couples' addresses very near each other?

parts.words: Retired couples' addresses very near each other?
parts.note: it looks like elderly pensioners living next door, but retired means gone to bed and addresses are things said to one another lying close

explanation.surface: Pensioner pairs who live close together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' here means gone to bed, and 'addresses' are speeches, not homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate conversation between lovers in bed is what the cryptic reading describes.

clue.text: Fleet having men on board competing in this

definitions.text: Fleet having men on board competing in this

parts.note: fleet as an adjective means fast, giving speed
the pieces moved on a chequered board are chessmen, pointing to the game

explanation.surface: A navy with sailors aboard taking part in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' reads as ships and 'men on board' as crew; really fast play with chessmen. The whole clue also describes the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed chess is the game played with short time limits, so players are quick while moving pieces.

clue.text: Use stand-by after damaging smartest suit, say

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are damaged and reformed

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a spare suit after ruining your best one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaging' mixes up USESTANDBY; 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One's finest clothes kept for church on the Sabbath; a smart suit is one example.

clue.text: Is this a help to see the light?

definitions.text: Is this a help to see the light?

parts.words: Is this a help to see the light?
parts.note: seeing the light sounds like a conversion or revelation, but a light is a crossword entry, and the thing printed to help solve it is meant

explanation.surface: A question about what helps someone have a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a 'light' is an answer in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Each grid entry has a hint printed beside it, the solver's aid to working out that entry.

clue.text: Eg, Gandhi till shot

indicators.note: shot as in ruined or knocked to pieces, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Gandhi, for instance, was a guiding figure until he was assassinated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges EGGANDHITILL; the whole clue also describes Gandhi, an inspiring figure until his assassination in 1948.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent, inspiring figure in a movement is a leading light, as Gandhi was in Indian independence.

clue.text: Article's wrong at first — journal's not for publication

indicators.note: wrong comes before the article, at its front

parts.note: milk that has gone wrong is off
the definite article is the
a journal is a record of events

explanation.surface: A newspaper item is wrong in its opening; the paper isn't printing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' places OFF ahead of THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks made to a journalist on condition that they are not reported or attributed are given unofficially.

clue.text: Small British chapel built for the Queen, London, 1926

indicators.note: the letters are assembled into a new structure

parts.note: British shortened gives Brit

explanation.surface: A little British chapel was put up for the Queen in London in 1926.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' rearranges BRITCHAPEL. Queen Elizabeth II was born in London (Mayfair) in 1926.
explanation.definitionFit: London in 1926 is where and when Elizabeth II was born, so the definition is an example of her place of birth.

clue.text: Have a stab at a rehearsal

definitions.meaning: to pierce with a sword or blade, literally to stab
a practice performance going through a piece once

explanation.surface: Attempting something and also practising it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a stab at' sounds like 'attempt' but means literally stab.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierce with a blade is one sense; a quick practice performance is the other.

clue.text: Drug bust in pub — for being in possession of Ecstasy

indicators.note: the scrambled pub words are said to possess Ecstasy, holding its letter inside them
busted means broken, so the letters are smashed and remade

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drugs raid in a pub, after someone was found holding ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' reads as a police raid but rearranges INPUBFOR into IBUPROFN; 'being in possession of' then sets E inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common over-the-counter painkiller, so it is an example of a drug.

clue.text: Progress, holding an old-fashioned dance

indicators.note: fare keeps the other pieces held inside it

parts.note: to fare is to get on or progress

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped, so the letters of old are reshaped

explanation.surface: Moving forward while performing a dance from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' looks like one adjective meaning dated; split it, and 'fashioned' (shaped) works on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The farandole is a Provençal chain dance performed in a line, so it is a type of dance.

clue.text: Wife of aggressively tough man wanting fresh start

indicators.note: the opening letter is swapped for a new one

parts.note: butch describes a tough, aggressively masculine type

explanation.surface: The wife of a hard man wants to begin her life again.
explanation.walkthrough: In cockney slang 'my old Dutch' is one's wife (from duchess).
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch is cockney slang for a wife, from the phrase 'my old Dutch'.

clue.text: Jazz pianist needing to change backing almost completely

indicators.note: the letters are read backwards
all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: to mutate is to change

explanation.surface: A jazz pianist has to alter his accompaniment nearly entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like musical accompaniment but reverses MUTAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Tatum was a celebrated American jazz pianist known for virtuoso technique.

clue.text: Extremely rare stamp meeting fellow revives

indicators.note: only the extremes, first and last letters, of rare are used

parts.note: of the same stamp means of the same kind
Les is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A very scarce postage stamp meets a chap and brings him back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stamp' suggests philately but means sort or kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To relight a fire or reawaken feelings is to bring them back to life, so the word means revives.

clue.text: Harbour with dock shown by poster — a coastal feature

parts.note: a port is a harbour
to dock a ship is to land it
a bill is a posted notice

explanation.surface: A port with a dock advertised on a poster as a seaside attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: Portland Bill is a headland at the tip of the Isle of Portland in Dorset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Dorset headland is a promontory on the English coast, an example of a coastal feature.

clue.text: Sign up, say, to support poor

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first, holding it up

parts.note: poor work is bad

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A protester signs up to help the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign up' looks like enlisting, but 'up' belongs to 'say', and 'to support' places that piece beneath the first in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is an emblem or token worn to show membership, so it is a sign.

clue.text: Native Americans had to jump over one

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to hop is to jump
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Native Americans had to leap over somebody.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are a Native American people of northeastern Arizona.

clue.text: Somewhat cheeky toddler needing to be brought up

definitions.text: Somewhat cheeky toddler needing to be brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upward
only part of the words is used

explanation.surface: A rather impudent infant needs a proper upbringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' takes EKYT from cheEKY Toddler and 'brought up' reverses it. The whole clue also describes such a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyke is a mischievous small child, an impudent little one in need of discipline.

clue.text: Player back in touch

indicators.note: the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a tuba is played, so is a player in the sense of something that plays

explanation.surface: A footballer is back in contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests a sportsman but is the instrument TUBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that abut share a border, so they touch.

clue.text: Film hero repeatedly being smug

indicators.note: repeatedly means over and over, so the film hero's word is said a second time straight after the first

parts.note: the good guy in a film is the goody

explanation.surface: A film's hero keeps being self-satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostentatiously virtuous and self-righteous behaviour is the sense, close to smug.

clue.text: Reflect, having oriental dog docked

parts.note: E stands for east, the orient

indicators.note: docking cuts off the tail, the last letter

parts.note: a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about having an eastern dog's tail cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' removes the W of CHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound or light can be thrown back, so to echo is to reflect.

clue.text: This is all actor can portray about saucy love and anger

definitions.text: This is all actor can portray

parts.note: re means concerning, about
pert means cheeky or saucy
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
ire is anger

explanation.surface: An actor's range covers playing cheek, romance and rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The full range of roles or pieces a performer can play is their stock of parts.
